text: Explain how a distributed storage system maintains consistency during leader failure, network partition, replica recovery, and concurrent client writes. Discuss replicated logs, epochs, quorum decisions, failure detection, stale leaders, snapshot installation, and recovery ordering. Use concrete examples and state the assumptions that make each safety argument valid.

Analyze virtual memory behavior under a workload that mixes sequential scans with random access. Discuss page tables, translation lookaside buffer misses, major and minor page faults, replacement policies, NUMA placement, memory mapping, dirty-page writeback, and swap. Explain how each mechanism affects throughput and tail latency.

Design an efficient large language model inference engine. Discuss continuous batching, paged key-value caches, prefix reuse, prefill and decode scheduling, GPU memory pressure, CPU offloading, SSD staging, network storage, synchronization, fairness, and throughput. Identify correctness invariants and useful performance counters.

Explain transaction processing in a distributed database under concurrency and partial failure. Discuss multiversion concurrency control, write-ahead logging, isolation levels, deadlock handling, replication, checkpoints, crash recovery, admission control, and query scheduling. Compare the latency and consistency tradeoffs of the major choices.
